discussion_comments.comment_body: This duplicates existing code. `core/services/cloud-handoff/git-preflight.ts` (#15219) already normalizes the remote and checks the branch and upstream, and `createWorkspaceGitReader` in `workspace-manifest.ts` already reads remotes and refs. Please reuse those, or put this snapshot logic in core next to `git-preflight` instead of keeping a second git runner in the app.

Moved the snapshot/publication implementation into core beside `git-preflight` in merged #15371, and reused `normalizeGitHubRemoteUrl`. Desktop no longer owns a second Git runner. The core snapshot path still needs Git operations beyond manifest discovery, including an isolated index, captured tree, unpublished-history checks, and publication of the approved commit.

`shutdownSession` and `releaseSessionRuntime` both start with `beginTeardown`, `session.pluginCommandsClosing = true` and `emitTaskCompletedOnTeardown`, and both then abort an active turn, wait for `pluginCommandTail`, and shut down the agent, the runtime and the plugin sandbox, with near-identical comments explaining why. Please move the first three lines into `beginTeardown` and put the shutdown steps in one method both functions call. What is left in each function will then be the real difference: the status and end event `shutdownSession` writes, and the runtime release `releaseSessionRuntime` performs.

Done. `beginTeardown` now also sets `pluginCommandsClosing`, emits the `task.completed` fallback and aborts the active turn (it runs before teardown's first await, which is where the abort has to be), and `shutDownSessionRuntime` holds the plugin-tail wait and the agent/runtime/sandbox shutdown. `shutdownSession` is left with the persist wait, the status write and the `ended` event; `releaseSessionRuntime` with the release. Net −22 lines.

We have a number of config.outputMode === "json" type branches here already. Could we look at making a role interface and, at the start, new up a "Json outputter" or a "console outputter" or whatever we have so we don't have to keep threading these conditionals through the code?

Already this if-else shows some things don't make sense... like "verbose json" output doesn't print model provider info. IF those are orthogonal, the code should reflect that and have the verbosity flow to all outputters.

It is OK if some outputters ignore calls they don't care about, but it will help clarify what the purpose of these events are, like "this is the start of a session run", etc. by choosing good method names.

Thanks — I refactored the run path around a `RunOutputter` role (`JsonRunOutputter` / `ConsoleRunOutputter`) created once at the start of `runAgent`. The `outputMode` branch is now isolated to the factory; lifecycle output uses straight-line calls (`runStarted`, `runResult`, `runAborted`, etc.), and `verbose` is passed into both outputters. Verified `bun -F @cline/cli typecheck`, Biome on the changed files, and `run-agent.test.ts` (22 passed). Pushed in `f8405b5`.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
This is why boolean parameters are terrible. At the call site, it is impossible to know without scrolling what these mean; and if you mix them up, then no type error results.

It would be better to have something like:

`load({ refresh: true, background: true })`

You can handle defaults with a splat like:

```
args = { refresh: false, background: false, ...actualArgs }
```

Agreed, switched to an options object in 56021e0af: `load({ refresh: true, userInitiated: true })`, with defaults via destructuring (`{ refresh = false, userInitiated = false } = {}`), which does the same thing as the spread. The poll and focus listener now call `load({ refresh: true })`.
